title: Buerman's help and the plan to escape north
summary: Buerman warns him after seeing a woman dragged away, and offers to help him reach Sweden, Norway or Canada via Gothenburg and Iceland.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So, I said well -- I went there that next day and there was a woman protesting about her son. They took her son away and I said, well, I don't know nothing and she was saying who was no good and everybody so -- all of a sudden four soldiers come and grabbed the woman and took her out.
And this Hans Buerman come up and says I'm glad you didn't say nothing, Jacques. I couldn't have helped you.
And I say, well, I don't know nothing. I didn't have nothing to say and I stayed there. The British were bombing. The British were taking care of business. They were bombing and bombing and bombing.
I says, I would like to try to make it to Panama or any of the West Indian Islands or Sweden or Norway. He says yes, you can go to Sweden. They are going to take it anyway.
We going to take it man, you might get a ship go through Iceland; and you might -- and you leave from Gutenberg and /you might make Canada. I'll help you to do that.
